rows.citation: Beattie KA, Hill AP, Bardenet R, et al. (2018). Sinusoidal voltage protocols for rapid characterisation of ion channel kinetics. The Journal of Physiology 596(10):1813-1828.
rows.model_type: hERG1a potassium-channel kinetic model (Hodgkin-Huxley-style two-gate / Markov), voltage clamp in CHO cells; cardiac-oriented
rows.controlled_mutations: no - fits one channel model to recordings; the word mutations in the text means genetic mutations, not seeded model faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - 8 s sum-of-sinusoids training protocol plus square-step and action-potential-clamp validation protocols in the same cell.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - compares full current traces and derived I-V / time-constant summaries; voltage clamp, no spike-feature extraction.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - hand-designed compact information-rich protocol; algorithmic protocol-design optimisation is mentioned only as parallel work.
rows.heldout_evaluation: yes - model predicts over five minutes of independent protocols not used for fitting (held-out protocols, not held-out models).
rows.software: mirams/sine-wave https://github.com/mirams/sine-wave (BSD-3-Clause per GitHub API); Figshare archive 10.6084/m9.figshare.4704550.v5 cited in paper (not fetched)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Channel-level voltage-clamp parameter fitting. NeuroSem would instead detect behavioural change between versions of NeuroML neuron models under current clamp, using seeded faults, calibrated tolerances, greedy battery selection and held-out models. Shared idea: a short protocol can carry the information of long suites.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (10.1113/JP275733); Europe PMC core record and full-text XML (PMC5978315); gh api repos/mirams/sine-wave
rows.found_via: WebSearch OED voltage clamp query; Europe PMC hERG query; NCBI idconv; Crossref

rows.citation: Clerx M, Beattie KA, Gavaghan DJ, et al. (2019). Four Ways to Fit an Ion Channel Model. Biophysical Journal 117(12):2420-2437.
rows.model_type: hERG1a two-gate Hodgkin-Huxley ion-current model fitted to whole-cell voltage-clamp data (nine CHO cells)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares fitting methods on one model structure; no seeded model faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - conventional step protocols, a short rapidly fluctuating protocol, and an independent validation protocol applied to every cell.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - summary curves (steady states, time constants, I-V) versus raw current traces; no spike features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - empirically compares multi-protocol versus single short-protocol fitting; no algorithmic protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: yes - independent validation protocol plus cross-validation predicting other methods' fitting data; held-out protocols, not held-out models.
rows.software: CardiacModelling/FourWaysOfFitting https://github.com/CardiacModelling/FourWaysOfFitting (GitHub license field NOASSERTION); Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.3378030 cited in paper (not fetched); uses Myokit and PINTS per paper
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Asks which calibration method predicts best, not whether an edited model changed behaviour. NeuroSem's single- versus multi-protocol comparison targets regression detection of seeded faults with frozen tolerances and count/runtime-matched random baselines.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API; Europe PMC core record and full-text XML (PMC6990153); gh api repos/CardiacModelling/FourWaysOfFitting
rows.found_via: WebSearch title query; PubMed esummary; Europe PMC abstract

rows.citation: Lewi J, Butera R, Paninski L (2009). Sequential Optimal Design of Neurophysiology Experiments. Neural Computation 21(3):619-687.
rows.model_type: generalized linear model (GLM) of neural spiking responses; statistical encoding model, not conductance-based
rows.controlled_mutations: no - estimates parameters of a single GLM; no seeded model faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - adaptively chooses a sequence of high-dimensional stimuli during an experiment.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - uses GLM likelihood of spike responses rather than electrophysiology feature extraction.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - real-time selection of the stimulus maximising mutual information about GLM parameters.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - simulations compare parameter convergence against random non-adaptive stimuli; no held-out models or fault families (abstract read only).
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Online information-theoretic design for parameter estimation. NeuroSem would select a fixed compact battery offline by empirical fault-detection coverage over mutants of conductance-based NeuroML models. Both compare against random stimuli.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata and abstract); Europe PMC core record (PMID 18928364)
rows.found_via: WebSearch title/author query; PubMed esummary; Crossref

rows.citation: Pillow JW, Park M (2016). Adaptive Bayesian Methods for Closed-Loop Neurophysiology. In: Closed Loop Neuroscience (Elsevier), pp. 3-18.
rows.model_type: statistical neural response models (nonlinear response surfaces, linear receptive fields) per Semantic Scholar auto summary
rows.controlled_mutations: no - available summary describes active learning for response-model estimation; no fault injection indicated (abstract not accessible).
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - closed-loop adaptive choice among many stimuli, per Semantic Scholar auto-generated summary.
rows.electrophysiology_features: unclear - abstract and full text not accessible; summary mentions response surfaces and receptive fields only.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - Bayesian active learning to choose stimuli in closed loop, per Semantic Scholar summary; details unverified.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - chapter content not accessible in this session.
rows.ai_transformations: no - nothing in available metadata indicates AI-assisted model edits.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Background on adaptive Bayesian stimulus selection for model estimation. NeuroSem targets offline selection of a regression battery for detecting edits to conductance-based NeuroML models; no mutation or held-out component is indicated here.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (book-chapter, pp. 3-18, ISBN 9780128024522); OpenAlex work record (author names); Semantic Scholar API (abstract elided by publisher, TLDR only); doi.org resolves to Elsevier linkinghub; ScienceDirect fetch blocked (403)

rows.citation: Shotwell MS, Gray RA (2016). Estimability Analysis and Optimal Design in Dynamic Multi-scale Models of Cardiac Electrophysiology. Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics 21(2):261-276.
rows.model_type: Hodgkin-Huxley-type cardiac excitable-cell ODE model with multi-scale (single cell, propagation, voltage clamp) simulated experiments
rows.controlled_mutations: no - discusses two deliberate model modifications to improve estimability, not seeded faults or mutant detection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - three simulated procedures: single-cell stimulation, action-potential propagation, and voltage clamp.
rows.electrophysiology_features: unclear - sensitivity and information-matrix analysis of simulated outputs; no spike-feature library evident in text reviewed.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - D-, E- and A-optimality criteria to weigh combinations of experimental procedures; criterion choice changes each experiment's contribution.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - simulation-based estimability analysis without held-out models or validation split evident.
rows.software: R Code Supplement distributed with the article (publisher supplementary material; not fetched)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Fisher-information design for parameter estimability. NeuroSem would choose protocols by empirical detection coverage of seeded single faults under calibrated tolerances, evaluated on held-out neuron models and a held-out mutation family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API; Europe PMC core record (abstract, PMC4906545); NCBI E-utilities efetch PMC full text
rows.found_via: Europe PMC refined OED clamp query; abstract via Europe PMC

rows.citation: Groenendaal W, Ortega FA, Kherlopian AR, et al. (2015). Cell-Specific Cardiac Electrophysiology Models. PLOS Computational Biology 11(4):e1004242.
rows.model_type: conductance-based guinea-pig ventricular myocyte action-potential ODE model (cardiac)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - genetic-algorithm parameter fitting with computational feasibility check; GA mutation is an optimiser operator, not model faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - stochastic current-clamp pacing combined with multi-step voltage clamp; adding voltage clamp improved some conductance estimates.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - fitting error on action-potential and current traces; no standardized feature-extraction library evident in text reviewed.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - hand-designed protocol combination argued to improve identifiability; no algorithmic protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - assesses prediction of dynamics not used in fitting (e.g. voltage-clamp-only fits predicting stochastic pacing); no held-out model set.
rows.software: none released identified; RTXI (rtxi.org) used for acquisition per paper
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Uses dynamically rich multi-protocol data to fit cell-specific models. NeuroSem would use multi-protocol batteries to detect behavioural drift between model versions, with seeded faults, frozen tolerances, greedy selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004242) and Crossref bibliographic query; Europe PMC core record and full-text XML (PMC4415772); input Semantic Scholar ID not confirmed (API 429)
rows.found_via: WebSearch Groenendaal identifiability query (Semantic Scholar page URL); Crossref title query did not match
